channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
item.description: Ambient SFT replaces standard supervised fine-tuning by adding a regularization objective requiring the fine-tuned model's high-temperature conditional distributions to match those of a frozen copy of the pre-trained model, with temperature interpolating between pure SFT (T to infinity) and full knowledge distillation (T = 1). The cost is a frozen reference model held in memory alongside the trainable model and additional logit computations per training step, comparable to standard distillation overhead, plus a temperature hyperparameter that must be tuned. It can fail if the pre-trained model's distribution is poorly calibrated for the target domain, if the temperature is mis-set (too high reverts to SFT's overfitting, too low propagates the teacher's noise), and the reported gains are relative improvements over SFT rather than absolute capability claims, so results may be marginal when the fine-tuning set is already large or diverse. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Optimize the Cob, Then the Kernel: Optimizing Beam Search for Generative Recommendation Inference
item.description: The method replaces vLLM's per-beam batched decoding and per-step engine invocations with Tree Attention that concatenates beams along the sequence dimension to share the prompt prefix KV, plus pre-generated partial-attention masks, static KV cache allocation, loop-unrolled dispatch, TorchAir graph compilation, operator fusion, and vocabulary-constrained decoding, all without custom kernels. The cost is substantial serving-stack reengineering tied to specific compilation tooling (TorchAir, Ascend NPUs) and reduced flexibility: static KV allocation and fixed short outputs assume the GR pattern of long prompts and few generated tokens. It can fail when the workload is general LLM serving with variable-length outputs or narrow beams, when porting to GPU/vLLM stacks where TorchAir compilation does not apply, or when memory headroom cannot accommodate the concatenated-beam sequence. 0 independent implementations, 33 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Implementing Binary Transformers with Approximate Memories with Permutation Invariance Enabled Selective (PIES) Protection
item.description: The technique replaces conventional error-correcting-code (ECC) protection of binarized Transformer weights in approximate (voltage-scaled) memory with selective protection of critical weights, grouped by exploiting row/column permutation invariance. It costs a preprocessing and grouping step plus protection metadata, but only on a narrow slice of weights, so overhead is lower than full ECC; it presupposes weight binarization, with its associated accuracy trade-off. It can fail if the deployment memory is not actually approximate or error-prone (commodity DRAM already includes ECC, yielding no benefit), if the permutation grouping misidentifies critical weights for a non-BERT architecture, or if error patterns deviate from the simulated uniform bit-error model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
item.description: QDA replaces manual, expert-driven selection of post-training quantization recipes with an LLM agent that iteratively builds candidates from a library of interoperable public PTQ methods and scores them in minutes via output KL divergence from the original model on held-out reasoning traces, with long-generation checks for failures such as repetition loops. The cost is roughly 64 GPU-hours of search per model-precision pair plus the engineering dependency on the released library, evaluator, and harness; checkpoints themselves run on existing serving kernels with no inference overhead. Failure modes include overfitting the recipe to the KL-based proxy rather than true downstream accuracy, silent failures on long generations that the checker misses, and infeasibility of quantizing very large models on a single 24 GB GPU without offloading or rented memory-rich hardware. 0 independent implementations, 15 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
item.description: Replaces uniform sub-4-bit weight quantization (and trial-and-error mixed-precision search) with a structured recovery waterfall that selectively restores INT8/FP precision to the roughly 5% of layers—late-stage pointwise projections and depthwise layers—where collapse concentrates. Costs added per-layer sensitivity analysis and a mixed-precision runtime; accuracy is recovered but storage savings shrink slightly and, critically, standard CPU runtimes incur a 1.48x–21.5x slowdown from software bit-unpacking, so memory footprint improves while edge throughput can worsen. Can fail if the deployment stack lacks native sub-4-bit kernels (the slowdown dominates), if the reader's backbone differs enough that the identified critical layers do not transfer, or if batch-size assumptions mismatch the reported latency figures. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FACT: Fixed-Budget Allocation and Cross-Step Training for Speculative Decoding
item.description: Replaces static, fixed-width draft candidate allocation in speculative decoding (and uniform detached drafter training) with confidence-guided tree allocation under a fixed node budget and cross-step training weighted toward early tokens. Costs the training and maintenance of a lightweight feature-prediction drafter plus allocation logic, with negligible extra memory relative to the frozen 8B target; no quality change under greedy verification. Speedups can vanish from host-thread or other execution-condition changes despite unchanged acceptance, proxy cross-entropy does not reliably rank drafters, and training and allocation gains do not necessarily compound. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Safe to Omit, Worth Omitting? Keeping the Answer and Cutting Latency When an LLM Agent Skips Another's Message
item.description: The method replaces unconditional waiting for a helper agent's message (text or KV cache) with a confidence-based gating rule that lets the receiver answer alone when a finite-sample test certifies that at most 5% of answers would change. It costs a calibration phase with labeled data per agent pair and task, the complexity of maintaining per-pair thresholds, and near-zero quality loss where certification passes; skipping KV cache yields far less time saved than skipping text. It can fail when the receiver's confidence is uninformative on a new distribution (certification simply fails and latency is unchanged, as on GSM8K), when answer parsers misjudge equivalence, and because text messages that merely perturb rather than inform can mask the fact that the helper adds no real accuracy. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Finetuning VLAs for Dexterous Manipulation: The Right Checkpoint Is All You Need
item.description: The technique replaces naive SFT-checkpoint selection (choosing by SFT rollout success) and full-model or LoRA fine-tuning of VLAs for dexterous hands with a recipe that freezes the VLM, fully trains the action expert, and selects checkpoints by post-DSRL steerability. Its cost is access to a pretrained VLA such as pi_0.5, a dexterous platform like the LEAP hand, demonstration data, and an additional diffusion-steering RL stage, none of which fit a single 24 GB GPU production budget. It can fail because the findings rest on two simulation tasks and one hand embodiment, SFT success is shown to be a poor proxy for steerability, and the recipe may not transfer to other VLAs, hands, or real-world deployments. 3 independent implementations, 251 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
item.description: MoMoVL replaces uniform-precision or modality-agnostic mixed-precision quantization of MoE-based VLMs with a bit-width assignment driven by per-expert activation profiles and per-modality (vision vs. text) quantization sensitivity. The cost is a modest accuracy drop relative to the uniform-precision baseline and the added complexity of computing modality-aware, per-expert bit allocations during compression. It can fail if the target model is not a sparsely-activated MoE VLM, if the expert-importance statistics do not transfer across workloads, or if the modest accuracy loss is unacceptable for the deployment task. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Same Rank, Different Needs: Rethinking LoRA Redistribution in Federated Learning
item.description: RASA replaces the standard leading-singular-direction truncation used to redistribute an aggregated federated LoRA update to each client with a receiver-aware readout computed from diagonal input second moments via uncentered PCA, plus a spectral-reference aggregation step that removes the personalized initialization offset. The cost is computing and communicating compact per-client second-moment statistics and performing a weighted eigendecomposition per round, which the authors describe as modest overhead. It can fail when the diagonal approximation of input second moments misrepresents the true response geometry, when client statistics are noisy or privacy-constrained, and the reported gains are confined to federated heterogeneous settings and do not transfer to single-node fine-tuning. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sightline: Long-Window Speculative Decoding for Fast SVG Generation
item.description: Sightline replaces standard autoregressive decoding (and short-window speculative decoding) for SVG generation with a block drafter whose verification window matches the drafter's horizon, filled by a wide draft tree. The cost is the added draft-model memory and compute per pass, a wider draft tree, and implementation complexity; lossless verification means quality is preserved by construction. It can fail to deliver gains if the drafter's acceptance rate collapses on out-of-distribution inputs, if the draft model cannot fit alongside the target model on a 24 GB GPU, or if workloads are latency-bound by factors other than token count. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
item.description: COTEX replaces full fine-tuning of a multimodal agent when adding a new specialist vision tool: it trains small adapters constrained to directions that trigger the call and select the tool without disturbing existing tool choices, plus a protocol that converts task-specific annotations into verified tool-use trajectories. The cost is adapter-level training and the engineering of the trajectory-verification pipeline; it requires a locally trainable open agent rather than a closed API model. It can fail if the verified trajectories are noisy or unrepresentative, and the orthogonal constraint does not guarantee zero interference, so existing tool behavior must be re-validated after each extension. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
item.description: The technique replaces purely test-pass-driven autonomous coding loops with in-flight feedback: after each code-changing turn, short messages naming functions exceeding a cyclomatic complexity limit or changed lines skipped by tests are injected into the agent's context. The cost is minimal infrastructure (standard complexity and coverage instrumentation plus extra context tokens per turn) and a modest increase in trajectory length as the agent spends steps refactoring. It can fail if the agent performs superficial refactors that game the metric without improving maintainability, if coverage feedback pushes it to write low-value tests, or if the added turns consume budget on tasks where complexity accumulation is not the binding constraint. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: NarrowSpec: Draft Hidden Width Need Not Match the Target in Speculative Decoding
item.description: The method replaces full-width hidden-state draft models in speculative decoding (DFlash, EAGLE-3) with drafts whose residual stream runs at half or a quarter of the target's hidden width, folding the output adapter into the borrowed vocabulary projection so logits are unchanged up to rounding. The cost is training a new narrow draft per target model and accepting a small reduction in token acceptance, which the reported end-to-end speedups indicate is outweighed by cheaper draft passes. Adoption can fail if no trained draft exists for the reader's target model, if serving stacks do not yet expose this configuration, or if acceptance-rate degradation at the reader's temperature, domain, or batch regime erases the latency gain. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
item.description: RoboBuilder is a benchmark in which coding agents co-design robot hardware and control programs, using real-world video feedback to correct simulator errors; it replaces pure simulation-based robot design with a sim-to-real closed loop. It costs substantial physical infrastructure: 135 robots built over an estimated 240 hours, plus fabrication and testing equipment. Its findings show simulation alone is unreliable (none of 15 initial passing designs crossed the real course) and 66% of simulated passes hold in reality, which is relevant only to robotics work. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Neural Memory Orchestration
item.description: Overseer replaces kernel heuristic prefetchers with a learned page-prefetching pipeline: an eBPF fault collector, a transformer predictor (OverNet) running on network-attached inference hardware, and a kernel enforcer that prefaults predicted pages into the target process. Its costs include dedicated inference hardware, kernel-level modifications and their operational risk, and the latency budget between fault observation and enforcement, plus per-instance feature engineering (ordinal ranks over deltas) to avoid per-workload retraining. It can fail on workloads whose access patterns are not learnable, when network or inference latency exceeds the prefetch lead time, on mispredictions that waste memory bandwidth and evict useful pages, and the reported gains come from only two fault-heavy workloads whose irregularity may not resemble the reader's inference workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
item.description: The method replaces expert-built per-device calibrated digital models and gradient-free trial-and-error for in situ training of optical neural networks, substituting a coding agent that probes the hardware through a camera-based harness with mandatory hypotheses. Its cost is agent inference plus repeated physical measurements, and it requires optical hardware, a camera interface, and a suitable harness that the reader's infrastructure does not include. It can fail through the agent forming an incorrect physical model of the device, slow convergence from measurement-by-measurement probing, and dependence on future improvements in LLM capability. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
item.description: The technique replaces human-annotated reward/evaluator training with a self-improving loop: controlled video edits (temporal reversal, frame dropping) create a proxy exam, per-dimension LLM agents propose updates, and a leader agent with a Nash bargaining rule balances gains across dimensions, with humans designing the exam and reviewing candidates. The cost is orchestration complexity, a hand-built evaluation curriculum, a small human-labeled anchor set, and repeated multi-agent optimization rounds around an 8B VLM. It can fail if the synthetic edits do not track real perceptual defects, if per-dimension tradeoffs stall bargaining, or if gains overfit the proxy exam rather than human judgment on new content. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction
item.description: The method replaces direct conditioning of agent actions on static psychometric profiles with a profile-conditioned world model that learns discrete transition codes from observed state transitions, using a posterior encoder during training and a prior at inference. The cost is a bespoke training pipeline (posterior/prior encoders, vector quantization, next-state prediction) plus dependence on environment-behavior transition data from simulators such as VEET or AgentSociety, with the evaluation limited to 313 participants. It can fail when deployed outside controlled simulators: the authors explicitly disclaim causal psychological mechanisms and calibrated long-horizon dynamics, so predictions on real users or long horizons may be unreliable, and the discrete-code components contribute mainly to Top-3 and distributional metrics rather than primary accuracy. 2 independent implementations, 63 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks
item.description: DFC replaces the fixed sparsity coefficient in generator-based sparse adversarial attack training with a per-epoch feedback controller that adjusts the coefficient based on the gap between observed hard-mask density and a target density, without changing the generator architecture or loss. The cost is minimal: a density computation and coefficient update once per epoch, with no extra memory or inference overhead. It can fail to help when the attack constrains perturbations to source-model feature-importance regions, as the paper reports no consistent gain for EGS-TSSA, and gains may not hold at densities far from the tested 10% target. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
item.description: Replaces unguarded general-purpose LLM data-analysis agents, where model-chosen statistical methods go unchecked, with a LangGraph pipeline combining reusable skills and symbolic diagnostic validation that can accept, override, or fall back on proposed methods. Costs include orchestration complexity (LangGraph dependency, skill library maintenance, diagnostic rule authoring) and added latency from validation and potential replanning loops. It can fail if diagnostic rules are incomplete or miscalibrated, causing incorrect overrides or rejections of valid methods, and the paper provides only case-study evidence, so reliability gains are not quantified. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect -- KV Cache Management for AI Agents
item.description: TripleKV replaces reactive KV-cache eviction and on-demand SSD retrieval in multi-tier serving stacks (e.g., vLLM extended with DRAM/SSD tiers) with tool-aware latency prediction that prefetches KV blocks into host DRAM before the agent returns from a tool call, plus deduplication of GPU-resident blocks and a victim cache that refills evicted blocks from SSD. The cost is systems complexity: it requires a custom three-tier cache manager, a per-tool latency predictor that must be trained or calibrated per workload, and additional host DRAM capacity, none of which is available when inference runs on a single GPU or behind third-party APIs. It can fail when tool-completion predictions are wrong (prefetches arrive too late or waste DRAM bandwidth), when workloads are not agentic or lack predictable tool boundaries, and at low concurrency where the KV working set already fits in GPU memory and the mechanism adds overhead without benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
item.description: Replaces summarization, masking, and structured or embedding-based memory with an append-only plain-text history log and a regex search tool for on-demand recall. Costs storage of the full unabridged history, extra tool-call latency and prompt tokens per search, and, in the paper's setup, reinforcement learning on the agent model to teach effective grep usage. Can fail when relevant facts cannot be matched by literal patterns (paraphrased or implicit information), when logs grow large enough to make searches noisy or expensive, or when an untrained model issues poor queries and under-retrieves. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models
item.description: The framework (PREM/Before the Choice) replaces informal decodability claims about prospective representations with a structured evidential protocol featuring preregistered probes, matched controls, and dependence-aware null models; it does not replace any production component. Adoption costs only experimental design effort, but the method targets interpretability and AI-welfare research questions, not inference or training pipelines. Its own results demonstrate the failure mode it warns about: probes can fail to decode unchosen trajectories, and reconstruction-by-elimination artifacts can invalidate apparent positive signals. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research
item.description: Agentic multiverse analysis replaces manual specification-curve robustness checks of empirical analyses with autonomous coding agents that enumerate analytical forks, validate them against a rubric, execute the specification grid, and cross-examine each other's outputs. It costs tens of dollars and hours of agent time per paper via third-party APIs, but adds orchestration complexity including rubric design, separation-of-duties enforcement, and fork-space validation. It can fail when agents converge through imitation of exemplar reports rather than independent analysis, when the enumerated fork space is narrower than what human analysts would consider, or when the validity rubric admits weak specifications that inflate apparent robustness. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Process-Knowledge-Guided Latent Diffusion for Generative Design of Porous Architectures: A Case Study in Aerosol Jet Printing
item.description: The technique replaces unguided or domain-only conditioned latent diffusion sampling for porous layout design by adding a ControlNet domain branch and a separately trained score regressor whose gradients steer each denoising step toward process-suitable layouts. It costs training and maintaining a VQ-VAE, a topology U-Net, a ControlNet branch, and a surrogate regressor, plus a process model for the score, and guidance at high weights requires tuning (score improved only past weight 300, with 12,000 needed for the reported gain). It can fail if the surrogate regressor mispredicts scores on noised latents, if the flow-focusing process model misrepresents actual deposition, or if results from seven modeled flow settings and four evaluation domains do not transfer to other processes or geometries. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
item.description: FI-ITEP replaces size-based heuristics for setting per-table pruning ratios in in-training embedding pruning with feature-importance-guided ratios. The cost is the computation of feature-importance signals plus the existing complexity of in-training pruning infrastructure, which the authors state is minimal but nonzero. The method can fail if feature-importance estimates are noisy or shift during training, misallocating pruning ratios and degrading accuracy, and the reported benefits were validated on recommendation workloads whose scale and sparsity patterns do not transfer to general LLM serving. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
item.description: The result replaces any assumption that static guardrails, blacklists, whitelists, or certifications can verify that an LLM-coupled agent will not execute a dangerous (or semantically equivalent) program; it substitutes a risk-management stance in which safety is enforced through layered runtime controls, sandboxing, and monitoring rather than verified in advance. It costs nothing computationally to read, but operationally it implies accepting residual risk and investing in defense-in-depth, since even bounded versions of the verification problem are PSPACE-complete and safety does not compose across agents. What can fail is any single-point safety mechanism: individually validated agents can jointly produce unsafe behavior, and equivalence-based evasion can bypass pattern-based filters. 3 independent implementations, 2211 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
item.description: ReLay replaces handcrafting analog layout generator libraries and direct LLM geometry generation by recovering generator programs from existing layouts, then promoting recurring constructions into an evolving reusable function library that LLM agents call instead of emitting raw geometry. Its cost is an up-front reverse-engineering and curation pipeline over layout corpora, dependence on specific PDKs and EDA tooling, and benchmark coverage limited to 1,050 layouts across 27 circuit families and three open-source PDKs. It can fail when held-out layouts contain constructions not yet promoted to the library (learned functions cover only 53-66% of calls), when layouts embed tacit designer intent that geometry recovery misinterprets, and when proprietary PDKs or DRC rules differ from the open-source settings evaluated. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
item.description: The technique replaces trusting LLM-agent self-generated tests and reviews with a verification-gated workflow: gates must kill tool-selected netlist mutants and fault replays, reviews are module-scoped, and formal checks guard custody invariants. It costs substantial extra engineering effort: building mutant harnesses, specification-derived tests, pre-registered replays, and formal properties on top of normal simulation. It can still fail because even the improved gates killed only 74% of fresh mutants, unscoped review is unreliable, and planted custody flaws evade review unless an explicit formal check exists for that invariant. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
item.description: The method replaces codebase-centric iterative optimization in autonomous ML research agents with an explicit Problem State that tracks blocking problems, candidate solutions, and controlled hypothesis tests. It costs substantial additional LLM calls and wall-clock time (24-48 hours per task) plus the engineering complexity of state tracking and research-note generation. It can fail when the initial problem analysis misidentifies the true bottleneck, causing hypothesis testing to reinforce a wrong solution region, and its gains may not transfer from MLE-Bench-style tasks to a given production workload. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
item.description: It replaces RL/SFT weight updates for domain specialization with evolutionary optimization of the agent harness (system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, planning scaffolding) around a frozen policy, using GEPA as the outer-loop optimizer. Cost is inference-time reflection and evaluation rollouts for the evolutionary loop, no GPU training; harnesses are loadable per domain and compose with later weight-based RL. Risks: gains depend on having a reliable task evaluator and sufficient trajectory budget, evolved harnesses may overfit to the benchmark-like evaluation distribution, and the paper itself finds weight updates still give the strongest single-path gains, so harness-only specialization has a ceiling. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
item.description: ChainAgent replaces two-stage pipelines that find vulnerabilities in isolation and assemble attack paths afterward with a goal-directed LLM agent that grows an exploit graph, searching backward from unmet preconditions and forward from discovered capabilities. It costs LLM API calls for iterative source-code inspection plus integration of the graph representation and PHP-specific chaining knowledge, with no training or special hardware required. It can fail through missed chains (recall is only 42-45%), false exploit paths requiring manual triage, and limited coverage outside PHP or outside the vulnerability and gadget classes in its empirical study. 0 independent implementations, 2077 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Coordinate Basis Linear Bandits with Sublinear Regret over Low-Rank Clusters
item.description: CBL replaces full O(d^2) covariance updates and fixed-rank sketched approximations (e.g., SOFUL) in high-dimensional linear bandits with clustered exact-orthonormal-basis representations plus sentinel-based cluster switching. It costs the bookkeeping of multiple clusters, per-cluster bases, and a tunable rank bound l, with per-round cost O(r_bar^2) instead of O(d^2). It can fail to deliver savings if the data has high intrinsic rank, clusters are poorly formed, or the workload is not an online bandit problem at all, in which case the machinery yields no benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: DRVEXO-4B-Unified: Design and Evaluation of a Modular Speech-Vision System
item.description: It replaces a pipeline of separate ASR, LLM, and TTS components with one 4B self-contained checkpoint using a temporal residual speech connector, boundary-delimited incremental synthesis, and task-conditioned scoring heads. The cost is adoption risk: weights and code are only planned for release, benchmarks are reported on validation sets without independent reproduction, and deployment needs a GPU capable of running a 4B multimodal model plus its audio encoders and decoders. It can fail on speech recognition robustness in noisy domains, on action-ranking accuracy for application-specific candidate sets, and on concurrency behavior outside the reported GB10 serving setup. 2 independent implementations, 798 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
item.description: MATE replaces direct execution of raw LLM-proposed mobile UI actions with a structured action record passed through a runtime guardrail (allow, block, or user-approval) plus predefined verified routes for recurring tasks, without modifying the underlying model. The cost is engineering effort to define the action schema, risk policies, verified routes, and post-execution screen checks, plus an approval step that adds user friction for flagged actions. It can fail when the guardrail's policy mapping misclassifies novel actions, when predefined routes break under UI changes in target apps, or when screen-context extraction is incomplete. 2 independent implementations, 2203 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
item.description: The approach replaces manual, iterative RAG pipeline engineering (chunking, retrieval, prompting, and reranking design) with an autonomous LLM coding agent that builds and refines the system in an open code space. Costs are frontier-model API spend over multi-hour agent runs, plus sandboxed execution infrastructure and task-specific evaluation harnesses to give the agent reliable feedback. It can fail when the reader lacks an automated scoring signal for the agent to iterate against, when the agent overfits to that metric, or when weaker models than the benchmarked frontier configurations produce systems below the human baseline. 1 independent implementation, 35 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents
item.description: DriftGuard replaces online counterfactual replay—re-executing agent trajectories per retrieved memory to detect drift—with an offline stage that builds causal supervision via paired counterfactual replays and trains a lightweight online risk model that scores memories from pre-action information. The cost is a substantial offline data-generation and training pipeline (repeated trajectory replays plus majority-vote aggregation into a memory drift score), while online inference overhead is small; no latency or accuracy figures are given in the abstract. It can fail when the offline counterfactual distribution does not match deployment-time attacks or tasks, when the learned risk model misses drift patterns absent from training, and in settings where the agent has no persistent memory or where building a replay harness over proprietary tool environments is impractical. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents
item.description: Tether replaces LLM-based monitors and stateless policy layers with runtime enforcement of formally verified stateful policies, inferred from system calls observed while executing each proposed action in an ephemeral sandbox. It costs per-action sandbox execution overhead and latency, requires writing and maintaining policies in an embedded Lean 4 DSL, and adds significant systems-integration complexity around syscall tracing. It can fail on attacks outside the modeled side-effect scope, on over- or under-permissive policy specifications, and when sandboxing is impractical for actions needing real environment state. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
item.description: Origin replaces manual cross-referencing of agent trajectory logs against source code during incident backtracking, substituting a cross-layer dependency graph, a query language, and a region inference algorithm to map high-level agent functionalities to function-call-level compromise entry points. The cost is engineering effort to build static taint-propagation subgraphs and region inference for each application, plus analyst time to issue queries; it neither prevents attacks nor reduces runtime overhead. It can fail when region inference mislabels functionality groups, when taint analysis misses dynamic or indirect flows common in agent frameworks, or when the limited application-level function call logs the paper acknowledges provide insufficient grounding for the mapping. 1 independent implementation, 12 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Stochastic Estimation of Transduced Language Models
item.description: Replaces threshold pruning with beam summation, which yields a lower bound with unknown error, with reweighted sampling without replacement for unbiased prefix-probability estimates. It requires recursive sampling with inclusion probabilities and a transduced language-model architecture outside typical LLM API or open-model stacks. Its applications are computational psycholinguistics, bioinformatics, and formal language theory rather than everyday ML engineering on small GPUs. 2 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
item.description: RoCoKV replaces static, attention-score-based KV cache eviction for reasoning traces with uncertainty-guided adaptive pruning plus redundancy-aware token selection, delivered as fused CUDA decode kernels in a vLLM plugin that keeps the paged KV layout and CUDA graph capture. It costs implementation and maintenance complexity of a custom kernel path, reduced effective cache capacity for uncertain reasoning phases, and potential accuracy risk if confidence-based pruning miscalibrates on out-of-distribution prompts. It can fail when attention scores mislead (the paper's motivating problem), when workloads are short-output where compression overhead is not amortized, or when the plugin diverges from the reader's vLLM release and breaks CUDA graph compatibility. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Towards Autoregressive Neural Network Parameter Generation
item.description: IGPG replaces random or task-specific weight initialization by quantizing pretrained network weights with a VQ-VAE and training a prefix-conditioned autoregressive generator to synthesize new parameters token-by-token. The cost is a full generative pipeline: a collection of pretrained models to learn from, VQ-VAE training, autoregressive training over weight tokens, and a subsequent adaptation or fine-tuning stage before the generated weights are usable. It can fail because the generated parameters are only initializations that still require adaptation, generalization to out-of-distribution architectures remains limited, and quantization plus generative mismatch can yield weights that underperform standard transfer learning from an existing pretrained checkpoint. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Reinforcement-Aligned Probabilistic Weather Forecasting with Discrete Tokens
item.description: WeatherCraft replaces continuous-state deterministic or diffusion-based weather forecasters (e.g., GenCast-style models) with a discrete multiscale token representation modeled by a causal Transformer, enabling direct ensemble sampling and GRPO-based alignment to downstream rewards. The cost is substantial: it requires training a domain foundation model on ERA5-scale data, building a multiscale tokenizer, and running RL post-training, none of which fits a 24 GB GPU or a limited cloud budget. Failure modes include tokenizer quantization errors degrading fine-scale fields, reward hacking against specific downstream metrics, and ensemble skill gains that may not transfer outside the evaluated benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
item.description: A²-VLA replaces manual affordance engineering and per-tool retraining of vision-language-action policies with an agent that hypothesizes task-relevant affordance features, validates them through autonomous simulation experiments, and conditions a π0.5 backbone on the extracted functional-region features. It costs teleoperated demonstrations per source tool, a simulation reconstruction pipeline, an autonomous experiment loop for skill refinement, and fine-tuning of the π0.5 backbone, all of which exceed a single-GPU budget once robot hardware is included. It can fail when reconstructed scenes diverge from real geometry, when affordance hypotheses do not transfer to tools with novel functional regions, or when the accumulated skill library biases extraction toward previously seen tool categories. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SiliconGym: A Versatile Reinforcement Learning Environment for Agentic EDA
item.description: SiliconGym replaces ad hoc, single-task EDA feedback loops with a cross-task RL environment built on versioned workspaces, budgeted execution, and acceptance-gated scoring, with streaming dispatch overlapping tool checks and generation. Adoption costs substantial infrastructure: access to open-source or commercial EDA backends (commercial licenses are expensive), stateful workspace management, and parallel rollout orchestration beyond a single 24 GB GPU's typical use. It can fail if open-source-trained rewards do not transfer, since paired netlist evaluation shows open-source PPA gains do not always survive commercial synthesis, making the learned policy unreliable on the production toolchain. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
item.description: GRODE-RTL replaces flat source-level context (or full synthesized-graph exposure) given to a tool-using LLM agent for RTL repair with a compact, hop-partitioned dependency view built from the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register, mapped back to editable source lines. Its costs are an EDA synthesis and netlist-to-source mapping pipeline, additional preprocessing latency per repair attempt, and the engineering complexity of maintaining that tooling, while the LLM itself remains an off-the-shelf API model. It can fail when the suspect register or anchor is misidentified, when faults span multiple clock stages beyond the extracted cone, and its evidence base is narrow: 30 faults and three specific models, so gains may not transfer to other designs, tools, or models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
item.description: CompAct-Bench evaluates LLM-based working-context compaction as a replacement for unbounded history accumulation in long-horizon agents, using controlled retention ratios across BrowseComp, SWE-bench, and an internal CompanyBench. Adopting compaction costs quality rather than infrastructure: even frontier models degrade downstream task accuracy under aggressive compression, and the iterative ratio-adjustment evaluation itself requires extra inference passes. After adoption, failures arise from distorted task state—unresolved issues rendered as conclusions and forgotten established results—causing incorrect decisions and redundant execution rather than mere information loss. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
item.description: STARK replaces flat episodic memory stores and retrieval-time episodic traversal with a dual-graph memory: an episodic graph of temporally, causally, and semantically linked events, plus an insight graph of LLM-extracted behavioral signals connected by the events that support them, with event-as-edge relational embeddings enabling cross-user transfer for cold-start users. It costs an LLM call per interaction for insight extraction and scoring, ongoing graph construction and maintenance, an embedding projection for transfer, and added system complexity relative to standard RAG-over-logs memory. It can fail through noisy or incorrect insight extraction that compounds as events accumulate, through embedding- or LLM-judge-based evaluation gains not transferring to the reader's domain, and through privacy or correctness risks when cross-user transfer infers insights for users with little data. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VR-SparseQuant: Accurate FP4 Quantization with 2:4 Sparsity on Vera Rubin
item.description: VR-SparseQuant replaces dense W4A4 activation quantization with 2:4 structured-sparse FP4 execution on Vera Rubin hardware, using overlapping sparse streams to refine high-error activations while keeping native FP4 throughput. It costs a one-time offline scale-ratio calibration plus custom shared-weight GEMM kernels that only exist for unreleased VRFP4 hardware; the accuracy recovery relative to dense RTN W4A4 is demonstrated on a single model. It can fail on models whose activation error distributions do not align with the 2:4 sparsity pattern, and the perplexity gain does not guarantee downstream task quality. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
item.description: FaithDetector replaces manual review or blind acceptance of coding agents' work reports with an automated classifier that flags unfaithful claims (misreported observations, misattributed evidence, overstated success, faulty explanations). It costs an additional verification pass per report, adding latency and compute or API calls on top of the agent run, plus integration effort into the existing workflow. It can fail through false positives that erode developer trust and through false negatives that let overstated success claims pass, and its reported macro-F1 may not transfer to agents or domains outside the SWE-chat sample. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Safety Rationales Hallucinate: Diagnosing and Grounding Multimodal Safety Guards
item.description: TCG-RL replaces outcome-only supervised or preference training of rationale-generating safety guards with a contrastive RL objective that rewards tool use only when it improves grounding over a tool-free reference. It costs an RL training pipeline (reward computation against a tool-free baseline, tool-execution environment) rather than simple fine-tuning, increasing training complexity and compute beyond what one 24 GB GPU comfortably supports. It can fail if the tool-free reference is a weak comparator, if tool coverage does not match the fine-grained attributes and relations where hallucination concentrates, or if grounding rewards degrade classification calibration. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Efficient and Robust Drafting with Multi-Token Prediction
item.description: The method replaces a standalone small autoregressive draft model (or single-token Medusa-style heads) in speculative decoding with a single shared multi-token drafting head that reuses the target model's KV cache via zero-copy cross-attention, target activation injection, and clustered vocabulary projection. The cost is additional draft-head parameters and a parameter-efficient fine-tuning step to keep the drafter aligned with the target model, plus implementation complexity in KV-cache sharing and verification logic. It can fail when the drafter drifts out of alignment under domain shift or on unusual inputs, since acceptance rates collapse and speculative decoding then adds verification overhead without delivering speedup; results are also demonstrated only on Gemma 4, so transfer to other backbones is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Sparse Low-Rank Biclique Decomposition for Graphs
item.description: Signed biclique decomposition replaces dense low-rank-plus-sparse approximations (e.g., robust PCA) of graph adjacency matrices with a sum of sparse signed binary rank-one factors plus a sparse residual, and can substitute cuSPARSE SpMM with factorized multiplication. The cost is a greedy decomposition pass whose quality depends on the gain-based heuristic, and the factored form adds implementation complexity relative to calling a standard sparse library. It can fail on graphs lacking strong shared-neighborhood structure, where few bicliques are found, compression collapses, and the factorized SpMM may be slower than cuSPARSE. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rank2Replace: VLM-Ranked Slot Replacement for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
item.description: Rank2Replace replaces standard training on raw images (or generic augmentation) with VLM-ranked, rank-preserving replacement of object-centric slots across images, so the small predictor learns to rely on task-relevant evidence rather than spurious cues. It costs a training-time pipeline dependency on pretrained VLMs and a frozen slot extractor, plus extra preprocessing and augmentation complexity, while inference remains unchanged and VLM-free. It can fail if the VLM misranks slot relevance, if slot extraction is poor on the target domain, or if the deployment shift differs from the benchmarked OOD splits, since gains are measured on only four datasets. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Harnessing Medical Visual-Language Models with Agentic Evidence Management
item.description: TUNE replaces the default agent pattern of passing raw segmentation masks directly to the model by explicitly managing which evidence to acquire, how to render it, and whether to accept the induced answer change. Its cost is added orchestration complexity and extra inference passes for presentation selection and update verification, rather than additional memory or training. It can fail when the harness accepts a mask-induced answer change that corrupts an initially correct prediction, and its gains may not transfer outside medical VQA domains with ground-truth masks. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting
item.description: ProtoCast replaces a monolithic neural weather forecaster with group-specific prototype banks, sparse mixtures of prototype-specific low-rank correction operators, and gated cross-group attention, jointly trained from scratch with prototypes refit each epoch. The cost is substantial: from-scratch training on weather datasets, per-epoch prototype refitting, and added architectural complexity that exceeds a single 24 GB GPU budget for global-scale data and offers no benefit outside weather forecasting. Failure modes include unstable prototype-operator associations during training, prototype banks that fail to capture rare regimes (as implied by the need for deletion analysis), and corrections that may not transfer across regions or variables. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces retrieval of raw interaction-history snippets with a trained writer that maintains belief records about the user, each carrying evidence, scope, and current-versus-outdated status, for a frozen agent. The cost is training and maintaining the writer model plus extra inference and record-management complexity at write time, since the target agent itself stays frozen. It can fail if the belief writer misjudges preference scope or staleness, if training tasks do not transfer to the deployed domain, or if the user base is too small or static to justify a trained component over simple history retrieval. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models
item.description: TCDA replaces the fixed denoising schedule of a diffusion language model with a task-calibrated schedule selected via simultaneous one-sided bootstrap bounds that certify utility and degeneration guardrails, deploying the cheapest certified candidate. It costs a calibration stage with paired data, candidate samplers, and bootstrap computation, plus a fallback to the full schedule when no candidate certifies; runtime overhead itself is minimal. It can fail if calibration data is unrepresentative of production traffic, if the utility tolerance or guardrails are mis-set (with false certification up to the nominal alpha, observed below 2%), or if unconditional generation comparisons are confounded by the ELF sampler's randomized time grid. 1 independent implementation, 159 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Kameleo: In-Situ Activation-Precision Selection for Bit-Serial LLM Accelerators
item.description: Kameleo replaces offline perplexity-driven calibration of per-layer activation precision with runtime in-situ selection on a bit-serial accelerator, using a local proxy that compares each GEMM's reduced- and full-precision outputs. The cost is confined to custom hardware: a two-pass precision-setting phase over the first tokens plus 3.7% accelerator area, with MXU prefill cycles reduced 2.11-2.34x at a 1% perplexity budget. It can fail where the local proxy diverges from global perplexity on out-of-distribution workloads, and its gains are inaccessible on commodity GPUs without the underlying bit-serial datapath. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models
item.description: FrontierReplay replaces fine-grained exact prefix caches for hybrid language models that must split the prefill pass at each mid-prompt checkpoint, instead logging a short window of recurrent-layer inputs during an uncut prefill and replaying them state-only to materialize checkpoints at predictable structural boundaries such as turn ends and branch points. Costs include buffering the logged input window, a custom cross-layer replay kernel, scheduler support for frontier-aware retention, and applicability limited to hybrid architectures with recurrent state; the replay itself is reported at 6-37x cheaper per token than recomputation. The approach can fail if reuse does not actually terminate at predictable structural boundaries (making checkpoint placement wasted), if the deployed models are pure-attention transformers where standard KV prefix caching already suffices, or if kernel and scheduler integration into an existing inference engine is unavailable or immature. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Complete-SVD: A Functional Norm Approach to Low-Rank LLM Compression
item.description: Complete-SVD replaces plain truncated SVD and prior output-aware weighting schemes for post-training low-rank LLM compression by minimizing a linearized, Kronecker-factored L2 logit-distance objective with a closed-form weighted-SVD solution, whose output-side factor is estimated unbiasedly from random probes. Its cost is K backward passes per calibration sequence (vocabulary- and length-independent) plus calibration data, and the compressed model still carries the quality loss inherent to the chosen rank ratio, with no measured inference speedup reported. It can fail when the linearization around original weights is inaccurate at aggressive compression, when the probe estimate is noisy at small K, or when calibration is unrepresentative, as the KL-SVD variant shows by improving calibration perplexity while degrading cross-corpus perplexity. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AscMLA: Unlocking FP4 Efficiency for Long-Context MLA Decoding through Asymmetric Scaling
item.description: AscMLA replaces dequantization or dual-encoding workarounds for FP4 KV caches in MLA decoding by applying asymmetric K/V scaling on a single shared FP4 latent with pipelined scale delivery. It requires hardware with efficient FP4 block-scaled kernels and an MLA-based model, and adds kernel-level implementation complexity rather than a drop-in change. FP4's narrow dynamic range can degrade generation quality on outlier-heavy activations, and the claimed gains may not transfer to non-MLA architectures or unsupported GPU backends. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
item.description: It replaces BF16 or higher-bit (4-8 bit) quantized serving of the model with a trellis-coded post-training quantization calibrated on BF16-generated agent session tokens, distributed as GGUF. It costs a one-time calibration on agentic traces, dependence on the authors' llama.cpp fork rather than mainstream inference stacks, and rules out the 2.0-bit checkpoint, which trails BF16. It can fail on agentic workloads whose tool-use patterns differ from the calibration distribution, and the matched-accuracy claim holds only for the two evaluated long-horizon benchmarks on this single model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
item.description: The technique replaces weeks of expert hand-crafting of routing, scheduling, and network-design algorithms with LLM-agent workflows that write, test, and iteratively improve solver code. It costs LLM inference (API spend or local GPU time) plus an execution sandbox with feasibility checking, and it may still require a licensed solver such as Gurobi as a reference or fallback. It can fail by producing infeasible or non-scaling algorithms on unseen instances: the best one-shot model matched Gurobi on only 39% of large instances, so iterative agentic loops and verification are mandatory. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Learning to Think with Images Faithfully via Adaptive Data Selection
item.description: It replaces fixed tool-use training corpora with adaptive selection of questions where zoomed evidence still changes the answer, supported by a small-object localization and verifiable-question synthesis pipeline plus an adaptiveness reward for tool-free answers when zooming is unnecessary. The cost is building and maintaining that synthesis and capability-estimation pipeline and running supervised or reward-based VLM training, which is nontrivial in data engineering and compute. It can fail if the synthesized questions or localization labels are noisy, if the capability estimate misclassifies which samples still benefit from zooming, or if the reward miscalibrates and suppresses genuinely useful tool calls. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
item.description: It replaces over-approximating taint analysis (every output tainted by every prompt placeholder) and costly second-model labeling with per-call data-flow summaries read from a single recorded forward pass, learned from labels and calibrated to a chosen missed-flow rate. Cost is one forward pass per analyzed call plus a labeled calibration set per call-site distribution; it adds an analysis dependency outside the model-serving path. It can fail under distribution shift (calibration guarantees hold only when deployment is exchangeable with calibration), and the no-reading-no-flow result is a first-order approximation that faint attention or sensitivity can violate. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
item.description: It replaces running every skill on every OS (or uniformly sampling executions) with a three-stage contract workflow: static screening for OS-sensitive evidence, targeted dynamic validation, and field-level repair of guide text, scripts, dependencies, or platform declarations. Costs are an added static-analysis and root-cause-review pipeline, plus residual dynamic runs; the absolute pass rate after repair remains only 38.4%, so most tasks still fail reviewer judgment. It can fail where OS assumptions are not visible in contract fields (runtime-only behaviors), where static evidence misprioritizes cases, and where repairs fix one platform while regressing another, since no cross-platform regression check is quantified. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beam Model Technical Report
item.description: Beam replaces dense frontier-scale models with a sparse MoE architecture that activates only 23.4B of 501.3B parameters per token, combined with FP8/NVFP4 quantization and speculative decoding for serving. Even fully quantized, the total parameter footprint far exceeds a single 24 GB GPU, so adoption requires third-party API access or substantial serving infrastructure, and the underlying training pipeline (10.5K GPUs, 23.8T tokens, 100M RL rollouts) is entirely out of reach. Failures can arise from MoE routing instability, quality degradation under aggressive NVFP4 quantization, dependence on a proprietary drafter model for throughput, and safety behavior (88.9% harmful-request refusal) that may not transfer to a given deployment's policy requirements. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
item.description: The technique replaces hand-written prompts or ad hoc trajectory logging with automatically mined, self-distilled guidelines injected into the agent's context at inference. Its cost is an offline lesson-mining and consolidation pipeline plus increased prompt length per call, with an added selection step for weaker models. Failures include high-support guidelines that backfire, provenance loss during consolidation, swallowed API errors masked by plausible logs, and evaluation confounds that can make a memory method appear better than it is. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs
item.description: HiSA replaces the full query-key dot product in RoPE attention with a static, parameter-free partial dot product over the hidden dimension, rather than sparsifying over tokens. The cost is that the model must be trained with HiSA from scratch (or with the provided FlashAttention-3 kernels); it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and it adds a custom kernel dependency. What can fail after adoption is portability and compatibility: gains depend on the custom FA3 kernel path, downstream fine-tunes of dense models cannot use it, and quality results are demonstrated on the authors' own training runs rather than established benchmarks at production scale. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies
item.description: UCMT is a causal discovery algorithm family intended to replace or augment standard structure-learning methods (NOTEARS, DAGMA, BOSS, RESIT, DirectLiNGAM) when inferring directed causal graphs from observational data. Costs include higher runtime than some baselines, added pipeline complexity from sparsity/BIC refinement stages, and compute for permutation-search comparisons; it does not require cluster-scale infrastructure and can run on modest hardware. Failures to expect: gains vanish under dataset-level multiple-testing correction in several regimes, orientation accuracy is modest (0.563 in the favorable ablation), arbitration and regime-selection components show no confirmed benefit, and there is no demonstrated broad advantage over RESIT, ANM, or DirectLiNGAM. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
item.description: ZeroVLN replaces navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of a VLM with a semantic tool-calling interface in which the frozen VLM brain issues natural-language movement decisions that a small action expert executes, with both policies then jointly improved via closed-loop reinforcement learning. The cost is an RL training pipeline in the VLN-CE simulator, an additional action expert to train and maintain, and extra latency from the slow-fast loop; the claimed benefit is avoiding degradation of the VLM's general capabilities. It can fail if the natural-language interface miscommunicates geometry, if RL-trained policies do not transfer outside the simulated environments, or if the RL compute exceeds a constrained budget. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
item.description: Seer replaces prompted self-evaluation and real trial-and-error exploration in deep-research agents with two offline-trained, agent-agnostic models: a tool-response simulator that imagines candidate outcomes and a value estimator that scores them, executing only the selected action. The cost is additional local inference compute for simulation and scoring, plus the one-time offline training of both models on a shared corpus of real research trajectories; no extra real tool calls are incurred for discarded candidates. It can fail when the simulator's predictions or the value estimator's scores are inaccurate, which the authors show limits the benefit of wider imagined search, and when the target tools or domains diverge from the training corpus. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management
item.description: MemFolder replaces naive record pruning and generic summarization in agent long-term memory stores: RecordFolder merges compatible records into fewer retrieval units via entity grounding, anchor selection, and temporal chaining, and ContextFolder further compresses records within each group using verification-feedback revision. The cost is additional offline LLM computation for grounding, anchor selection, encoding, and fact-recovery verification, plus pipeline complexity and a dependency on external memory benchmarks that may not match the reader's distribution. Failure modes include anchor selection that loses complementary evidence, entity grounding errors that corrupt group structure, and verification that passes while subtle facts are lost, degrading downstream answers silently. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MaskPE: One Mask, Two Roles: Weight Placement and MAC Gating in Systolic Arrays
item.description: MaskPE replaces conventional weight-stationary systolic PE placement and zero-skipping logic with mask-directed weight preloading and clock gating of arithmetic registers in zero-weight PEs. The cost is custom hardware: positional mask metadata, RTL redesign, and per-tile mask steering, with gains validated only at gate level rather than on silicon. For the reader it can simply fail to apply at all, since its energy and storage benefits exist only on custom accelerators, not on GPUs or third-party APIs. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Aggron: Aggressive Compression of Agentic KV Caches during Head-of-Line Stalls in the Request Queue
item.description: Aggron replaces threshold-triggered, bulk asynchronous context summarization with per-turn selective KV cache summarization scheduled into a separate queue that consumes idle compute and memory created by head-of-line stalls in the main request queue. The cost is substantial serving-stack complexity: a second queue, a predictor that issues summarizations only if they finish before the stalled request executes, and continuous per-turn summarization overhead, none of which is available in off-the-shelf engines or hosted APIs. It can fail when the completion-time predictor mispredicts (wasted summarization compute or late compression), at low load where head-of-line stalls are rare, or if selective summarization discards context the agent later needs, degrading accuracy on long-horizon tasks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Held While Waiting: What LLM Agent Sessions Reserve on Serverless and Agent Runtimes
item.description: The technique replaces the default one-reserved-environment-per-conversation model on serverless agent runtimes with explicit client-side session closing and, where the platform permits, multiplexing many conversations onto one environment; it replaces implicit 15-minute idle holds after a conversation ends. Closing costs only client-side lifecycle logic, while sharing costs platform support (largely unavailable in surveyed runtimes) and adds up to ~40 ms queuing delay for most replies; compute-per-reply figures of 5–40 ms are estimates the authors flag as hard to measure. Sharing can fail on isolation: environments hold model-selected tool and code execution, so multiplexing without adequate sandboxing risks cross-conversation leakage, and on platforms without sharing support, unclosed sessions will still exhaust the environment pool before CPU does. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
item.description: AutoMaster replaces Vanilla SFT on raw successful teacher trajectories with SFT on skill-guided trajectories, where an LLM agent analyzes failures, designs natural-language skill instructions, selects data, and retains skill context during fine-tuning. It costs an agentic pipeline for trajectory analysis, skill design, and iterative rollout-plus-evaluation feedback, plus the API or GPU expense of repeated teacher rollouts and target-model SFT, without reducing deployment cost. It can fail when the designed skills encode incorrect behavioral assumptions, when gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated terminal/search/SWE tasks, or when the reader's tasks lack verifiable evaluation signals to drive the autonomous feedback loop. 1 independent implementation, 148 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
item.description: The system replaces manual or AutoML-style feature selection with an LLM-agent loop that proposes cross features, blends multiple importance rankings, and tunes selections via 10–25 asynchronous trials under cost and QPS caps. The cost is substantial supporting infrastructure: deterministic experiment and verification tools, a shared feature pool at fleet scale, several importance-estimation methods, Pareto-front blending, and repeated offline evaluation, plus the API or serving cost of the agents themselves. It can fail when hypotheses are ungrounded, importance signals are noisy, the 10–25 trial budget is insufficient for the combinatorial space, or offline normalized-entropy gains do not transfer to online metrics. 0 independent implementations, 33 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
item.description: The method replaces passive incident catalogs and pass/fail benchmarks with offline multi-agent replications of reported incidents paired with matched controls lacking only the blamed cause, enabling root-cause validation. It costs the engineering effort to rebuild each incident environment and control, plus repeated agent runs across models, and the warning-based mitigation adds per-tool-output tokens without eliminating residual harm. It can fail because replication fidelity depends on incomplete media reports, results cover only five models and 108 incidents, hazard-naming warnings require knowing the hazard in advance, and defenses may not transfer to novel hazards or attacker-driven scenarios. 2 independent implementations, 2084 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
item.description: The technique replaces the manual hypothesis-implement-train-evaluate loop of ML engineers on large recommendation rankers with human-on-the-loop LLM agents that propose, code, train, and score model changes, with engineers retaining control of objectives and final review. It costs substantial parallel training capacity (1,097 completed experiments in one campaign), a carefully calibrated offline objective, and significant context and harness engineering around the model. It can fail because offline metrics do not reliably predict online impact, gains saturate after early wins, and the approach presumes experiment throughput and A/B testing infrastructure unavailable to small teams. 1 independent implementation, 158 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
item.description: It replaces full-feature executable GUI training environments with MobileGym-Lite, which retains complete reward and data coverage while pruning application features that the tasks do not use. It costs environment-engineering effort to identify and remove unused features, and it reduces environment construction cost while training a 4B vision-language agent, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail because the reported improvement is sensitive to episode weighting: the gain reverses under equal per-episode weighting and vanishes when pruned-task episodes are balanced, and single-reference-path verifiers degrade success by over ten points. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReCIM-HD: A 40 nm On-Device Learning Accelerator with Hyperdimensional Computing via Importance-Based Hybrid Digital-ReRAM CIM
item.description: ReCIM-HD replaces backpropagation-based on-device learning with gradient-free hyperdimensional computing executed on a custom 40 nm ReRAM compute-in-memory accelerator, using analog similarity search for class hypervectors and a small digitally protected subset to preserve accuracy. Its cost is custom silicon with a custom ISA and encoder, plus the accuracy limitations inherent to HDC classifiers, which are well below deep networks on complex modalities such as images and natural language. Analog ReRAM computation also risks device variability, conductance drift, and noise degrading inference accuracy outside the hybrid digital fallback path. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: OMNIS+: Semantic RAN Slicing and Quantization for Dynamic Split Neural Networks
item.description: OMNIS+ replaces static RAN slicing and fixed split-DNN offloading with dynamic split-point selection, adaptive 'box' quantization of intermediate features, and joint MD/ES optimization via multi-armed bandits and block coordinate descent. It costs a distributed multi-agent control stack (contextual MAB agents per device, Lyapunov queue control, per-server BCD resource allocation) plus integration with cellular RAN primitives such as MCS, cell association, and GPU frequency control. It can fail under partial observability or non-stationary network conditions where bandit estimates lag, and its error-resilience and QoS gains are validated only in simulated multi-cell settings that do not transfer to conventional server or API inference deployments. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
item.description: Intent contracts replace planner-written tool calls (optionally screened by a reviewer) with a logged goal-plus-quotation contract that validation code and a small trusted model convert into the actual tool call, confining the planner's influence to the contract. The cost is an extra trusted-model call per step, additional validation and dispatch code whose correctness the guarantees depend on, and the need to structure every action as a contract. It can fail on ambiguous references: once environment terms are clarified, state-changing conditions hit a wrong target in 40-49% of runs, because the trusted model cannot see the environment to check object choice, and it does not reduce unauthorized actions compared with blind review. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
